'''Jim Colson''' was one of Decipher's first [[Squadron Members]], listed as Gold 5 FL in the Dagobah region from Huntsville, Alabama.<ref name="decsq-dagobah" /><ref name="decsq-prof" /> The fan site's Squadron Members table marks him Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.<ref name="sm-fan" />

Council pages in December 2002, June 2004, and August 2005 title him Shadow Squadron Leader.<ref name="council2002" /><ref name="ss-council2004">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040603222905/http://www.swccgpc.com/council.htm Advocate Council], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 3 June 2004)</ref><ref name="ss-council2005">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050829220138/http://www.swccgpc.com/council.htm Advocate Council], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 29 August 2005)</ref> The June 2004 and December 2005 rosters list him as Shadow Leader in Huntsville, Alabama.<ref name="pc-vol04" /><ref name="ss-vol2005">[https://web.archive.org/web/20051203064943/http://www.swccgpc.com/volunteers.htm Shadow Squadron], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 3 December 2005)</ref> At the [[DecipherCon 2002]] award ceremonies on 3 November 2002 he announced the top places in the Star Wars CCG, Young Jedi CCG and Jedi Knights TCG World Championships, and thanked [[Warren Holland]] and Decipher for their support of the Players Committee over the past year, including the prize purses for the World Championships.<ref name="pc-nov02">[http://www.swccgpc.com/Archives/november02archives.htm November Updates], swccgpc.com (3 November 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030423221953/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/november02archives.htm Internet Archive]</ref> In February 2005 the online magazine ''[[dGamer]]'' listed him among its contributors.<ref name="dgamer-fp">[http://dgamer.red84.com/ dGamer - A Magazine for DECIPHER Gamers], dgamer.red84.com (23 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050223115202/http://dgamer.red84.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> In August 2006 the Players Committee Design Team had a long discussion with [[Michael Bahr]] and Colson about card availability and the prospect of cards becoming unavailable; Bahr then drew up the "Virtualization Market Guide", which gave every card a point value and listed cards the team should avoid virtualizing.<ref name="pc-sid94">[http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=94 Policy of virtualizing], swccgpc.com (15 August 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080906211140/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=94 Internet Archive]</ref>

As Shadow Squadron Leader, Colson handled the Players Committee's prize product. In November 2002 he wrote that the PC could put together a Chase the Can support package quickly, on approved request, for organizers willing to pay the shipping from the warehouse, which was "still a very manual effort";<ref name="pcf-228-3196">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=3196#3196 Chase the Can events?], Jim Colson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 November 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050221161054/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=2804%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> the product might be ''Menace of Darth Maul'' for [[Young Jedi]], Premiere for [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game|Jedi Knights]] or white-border Premiere for Star Wars CCG, and approval would rest on references or being a known entity.<ref name="pcf-228-3265">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=3265#3265 Chase the Can events?], Jim Colson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 November 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050221161054/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=2804%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In July 2003 he pledged that the PC would "FULLY support" a proposed Jedi Knights tournament effort with Jedi Knights prizes,<ref name="pcf-1858-30200">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30200#30200 Who wants a tournament?], Jim Colson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (2 July 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050228105408/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30194%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and he arranged uncut sheets matching each event's game (three Young Jedi, four Star Wars CCG) and packs as prize support for the seven sealed deck tournaments of the Vintage Stock Tour.<ref name="pcf-1895-30304">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30304#30304 Vintage Stock Tour! Uncut Sheet Prizes! 7 tournaments!], Freelancer, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (4 July 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041101152255/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30301 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-1895-30396">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30396#30396 Vintage Stock Tour! Uncut Sheet Prizes! 7 tournaments!], Jim Colson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (7 July 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041101152255/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30301 Internet Archive]</ref> On 6 October 2003 he announced that all uncut-sheet prizes for the 2003 State Championships, Nationals and Opens had been shipped: Light Side or Dark Side Endor foil uncut sheets, with international prizes sent by surface mail.<ref name="pcf-2267-34135">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=34135#34135 SWCCG States, Nationals & Opens Uncut Sheet prizes ship!], Jim Colson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040306022249/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=34203%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> He also wrote that he had given [[Andrew Howard]] about 100 uncut sheets after Gen Con 2003 for contest prizes.<ref name="pcf-2267-34203">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=34203#34203 SWCCG States, Nationals & Opens Uncut Sheet prizes ship!], Jim Colson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (10 October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040306022249/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=34203%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In September 2003 Shadow Squadron member John Anderson (Shadow 29) suggested him as a candidate for Tournaments Advocate,<ref name="pcf-2188-33321">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33321#33321 New Tournament Advocate], John Anderson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and on 4 November 2003 Colson introduced [[Mitch Velasco|Mitch]] as the new Tournaments Advocate.<ref name="pcf-2340-35270">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=35270#35270 New Tournaments Advocate!!], Jim Colson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (4 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040330200124/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=35280%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In 2004 Flight Leaders passed tournament directors' prize-package requests to Colson, who handled payment and shipment.<ref name="pcf-3378-46962">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46962#46962 Tournament Support], Nick Kolnik, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (31 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212746/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46962%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In October 2004 [[David Kangas]] wrote that Colson sat on the PC's product warehouse, sorting and shipping official prize support worldwide, and had often been "the backbone" of the World Championships.<ref name="pcf-4063-55368">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55368#55368 State of the PC Address: So long and thanks for all the fish], David Kangas, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 October 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050228234323/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=55374%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> His forum signature (captured March 2004) read "PC Advocate - Shadow Squadron Leader / Gold 5, Ambassador, Rider of Rohan".<ref name="pcf-2267-34135" />

[[File:Jim Colson DecipherCon 2000.jpg|thumb|right|220px|link=DecipherCon 2000|Colson at DecipherCon 2000]]

After [[DecipherCon 2000]] he played in the post-con hallway games recorded by Brandon Baity.<ref name="baity-hall">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hphw-Sjb5oQ DecipherCon 2000 - Post Con Hallway Gaming], Brandon Baity. Tagged still: [https://www.facebook.com/photo/?fbid=10237436742555504&set=a.10230980334389335 Facebook], Kevin Reitzel (8 July 2025). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012161816/https://www.facebook.com/plugins/post.php?href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Fkevin.reitzel%2Fposts%2F10237436825557579 Internet Archive].</ref> He answered Decipher's call for Squadron Members in 1996. For almost a year he was the only tournament director in a three-state area of Dagobah and Yavin 4, running monthly events in Huntsville, Birmingham and Nashville. He was also a Star Trek CCG Ambassador.<ref name="decsq-prof" />

== In their own words ==

<blockquote>
I was first introduced to CCGs by a friend of our family, who gave me my first Star Trek CCG starter deck. (They didn't even know how to play the game) I sat down and figured out how to play over christmas break in 1994. I played Star Trek CCG until Star Wars CCG came out.  I became one of the first Squadron members (Gold 5) when I responded to the Decipher "Call" 1996.

I was the first and only Tournament Director in a 3 state area of Dagobah/Yavin-4 for almost a year.  I ran tournaments in Huntsville, and Birmingham, AL as well as Nashville, TN every month.

I am also a Star Trek CCG Ambassador.  I collect LOTS of stuff, Cards, Action Figures (Old and new) Stamps and Coins and Boy Scout Badges. In my Free time, I volunteer as an Adult leader for the Boy Scouts of America and I also do volunteer work for my local Church with my lovely wife, Michelle, who I met while completeing my Engineering Degree at Texas A&M University.  In my "Real" life.. I work full time for the US Dept of Defense as an Engineer. I speak French fluently, and posses a BA in French along with my  Engineering Degrees. Michelle and I LOVE living here in
Huntsville, Alabama  Home of the US Space and Rocket Center - Space Camp USA!
                               Jim Colson<ref name="decsq-prof" />
</blockquote>

== 2022 interview ==
In a 2022 interview Colson said he came to SWCCG from the ''Star Trek'' CCG and pre-ordered six cases of [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]]. His first tournament, in Huntsville, drew two players who drove up from Tuscaloosa. His monthly circuit in Huntsville, Nashville and Birmingham included the first tournament [[Steven Lewis]] played. [[Kyle Heuer]] told him he had run more tournaments than any other Decipher volunteer.<ref name="colson">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=307s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 05:07. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=383s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 06:23. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref> He also ran events at Gen Con, DecipherCon and regional conventions, and he later became card games director at Dragon Con.<ref name="colson-0740">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=460s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 07:40. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref> At the end of the license period he visited Decipher's Norfolk offices as a [[Players Committee]] representative and took some boxes of material for the PC.<ref name="colson-2356">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=1436s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 23:56. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref>

Colson explained "Premiere Blue" cards as Premiere cards printed without the yellow ink. He said Cartamundi's Belgian plant was at capacity in the mid-1990s. The ''Star Trek'' CCG's first expansion, ''Alternate Universe'', spent most of a near year-long delay in customs. Moving some printing to PBM Graphics in the United States gave Decipher closer quality control.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=1652s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 27:32. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=1734s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 28:54. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=1848s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 30:48. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref> He said Premiere, A New Hope and Hoth were developed at the same time, and that volunteers playtested Endor about six months before its release.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=1995s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 33:15. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref> Before the license ended, Decipher consulted him about relic cards containing cut film cells, and it had discussed selling factory-graded cards.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=2367s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 39:27. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=2694s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 44:54. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref> He said the DecipherCon Corellian Corvette and Imperial-class Star Destroyer tournament foils were given one per attendee, and that leftover copies went into the next year's regional tournament kits. Reflections Gold was playtested only inside Decipher.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=3606s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 1:00:06. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=3849s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 1:04:09. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref> He said [[Defensive Shield|Defensive Shields]] were a middle path short of a second edition.<ref name="colson-2e-shields">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=939s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 15:39. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015174310/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]].</ref> That work "became moot" when the license ended.<ref name="colson-2e-shields" /> Asked what would have happened if the license had continued, he said there would have been a [[SWCCG 2nd Edition]].<ref name="colson-2e">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=4105s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 1:08:25. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015174310/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]].</ref> He said it would have used one card back, as later games such as [[WARS TCG]] did.<ref name="colson-2e-wars">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=4118s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 1:08:38. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015174310/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]].</ref>

== Collecting ==
Colson kept vinyl velcro convention-booth cards, including a Death Star and Chewbacca.<ref name="colson-velcro">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=1182s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], [[BoardMatt]], YouTube (24 April 2022), at 19:42. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015174310/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]</ref> An oversized [[Chewbacca]] convention-booth card in [[Andy Talaga]]'s collection came from Colson.<ref name="talaga-weird">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4dR5MIPH4h4 Star Wars CCG - Most Interesting and Strangest Things in Our Collections with Special Guest Andy], [[BoardMatt]] with [[Andy Talaga]] (29 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20220529152129/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4dR5MIPH4h4 Internet Archive]; [https://archive.org/details/youtube-4dR5MIPH4h4 Internet Archive item].</ref>
